item.title: DeepSpeed Expands with Training, Inference, and Compression Examples
item.description:
DeepSpeed Expands with Training, Inference, and Compression Examples

📚 Documentation and Examples

The DeepSpeed repository contains various examples including training, inference, compression, benchmarks, and applications that use DeepSpeed.

🏗️ Training and Finetuning

There are several training and finetuning examples so please see the individual folders for specific instructions.

🚀 Inference Options

  • The DeepSpeed-MII inference README explains how to get started with running model inference with DeepSpeed-MII and DeepSpeed-FastGen.
  • The DeepSpeed Huggingface inference README explains how to get started with running DeepSpeed Huggingface inference examples.

📦 Model Compression

Model compression examples are included in the repository.

📊 Benchmarks

All benchmarks that use the DeepSpeed library are maintained in a dedicated folder.

🎯 End-to-End Applications

This folder contains end-to-end applications that use DeepSpeed to train and use cutting-edge models.

🤝 Community Contributions

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. When you submit a pull request, a CLA bot will automatically determine whether you need to provide a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) and decorate the PR appropriately.

📜 Code of Conduct

This project has adopted the Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct.

🧩 Available Repositories

A markdown table lists the key DeepSpeed repositories with their functions:

Repository/Folder Purpose
DeepSpeed GitHub repository Core DeepSpeed library and examples
DeepSpeed-MII GitHub repository Model inference optimization
DeepSpeed-FastGen GitHub repository Fast generation for large models
Huggingface inference examples Inference examples using Huggingface
Benchmarks using DeepSpeed library Performance benchmarks
Training and finetuning examples Examples for training and finetuning models
Integrations Various integration examples

🔧 Key Details

  • Most contributions require a Contributor License Agreement (CLA)
  • You only need to sign the CLA once across all repos using this system
  • The CLA bot automatically handles status checks when submitting pull requests

item.title: EleutherAI releases GPT-NeoX 2.0 for large-scale language model training
item.description:
EleutherAI releases GPT-NeoX 2.0 for large-scale language model training

EleutherAI has announced version 2.0 of the GPT‑NeoX library, a framework for training massive autoregressive language models on GPU clusters. The update moves the codebase onto the latest DeepSpeed release and adds versioned releases for backward compatibility.

🔍 Overview

  • Implementation of model‑parallel autoregressive transformers on GPUs.
  • Built on NVIDIA’s Megatron Language Model and augmented with DeepSpeed techniques and novel optimizations.
  • Repository records EleutherAI’s library for training large‑scale language models on GPUs.

🧩 How it works

  • Employs model parallelism to distribute transformer layers across multiple GPUs.
  • Supports launch via Slurm, MPI, and the IBM Job Step Manager.
  • Executed at scale on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs on platforms such as AWS, CoreWeave, ORNL Summit, ORNL Frontier, LUMI, and CINECA Leonardo.

⚙️ Key details

  • Two versioned releases are provided:
    • Version 2.0 – built on the latest upstream DeepSpeed and maintained going forward.
    • Version 1.0 – snapshots of the older stack used for GPT‑NeoX‑20B and the Pythia Suite.
  • Prior to 3/9/2023, GPT‑NeoX relied on DeeperSpeed, which was based on DeepSpeed 0.3.15.
  • Leverages many of the same features as the Megatron‑DeepSpeed library but with increased usability and novel optimizations.
  • Not intended for generic inference; for inference‑only needs, Hugging Face transformers is recommended.

🚀 Availability & Adoption

  • More than 40 organizations in academia, industry, and government have used GPT‑NeoX to train over 50 models.
  • Notable model families include:
    • Pythia (EleutherAI)
    • StableLM (Stability AI)
    • RedPajama‑INCITE (Together.ai)
    • FORGE (Oak Ridge National Lab)
    • Sarashina1 (SB Intuitions)
    • TildeOpen‑30B (Tilde)
  • Evo 2 from the Arc Institute was trained with Savanna, a framework derived from GPT‑NeoX.
  • A full list of models and publications is maintained in USERS.md.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a centralized, accessible location for techniques that train large‑scale autoregressive language models.
  • Accelerates research into large‑scale training by offering a usable, versioned codebase and support for diverse HPC environments.
